https://shop.aeon.com/netsuper/ (requires iAEON ID login before any product/price is visible)
https://www.life-netsuper.jp/ (pure client-side app shell, no server-rendered product content, and login/postal-code gating)
https://search.rakuten.co.jp/ via direct HTTP fetch (Akamai bot-block, HTTP 403/reference-id page; worked fine when loaded in an actual browser session instead)
summary: WebSearch quota was exhausted early (shared across parallel country-research agents), and Oisix, AEON, Ito-Yokado and Life net-supers were all unreachable (bot walls, JS-only shells, or login/postal-code gates), so every observation instead comes from Rakuten Ichiba marketplace listings from individual greengrocer/farm shops, read live in a real browser session (search-snippet evidence with direct item.rakuten.co.jp product URLs). Japan's total-display-price law means listed consumer prices are tax-inclusive by default even when not explicitly marked 税込, and two listings used here state 税込 explicitly. Coverage reached 19 of 21 benchmarks across all six categories; only pea-shoots and a living microgreen tray were not found — fresh-cut sprouts/shoots are apparently too cheap and perishable to ship nationally on this marketplace, so only seeds and grow-kits are listed for them. Two microgreen benchmarks were filled with reasonable substitutes per the brief's 'any single microgreen pack' allowance (broccoli sprout for radish-microgreens, an unlabeled 'micro-leaf' mix for garden-cress-microgreens). A couple of root-vegetable listings (carrot, beetroot) are labeled 無農薬 (pesticide-free) rather than certified organic and were tiered 'premium' accordingly, and the carrot listing is a cosmetically-imperfect (訳あり) bulk bag.
